newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Bank Handlowy sell-off in H1 1997 - president.
newsitem.headline: Polish Bank Handlowy sell-off in H1 1997 - president.

text.p: Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski assured international investors on Thursday that the country's leading commercial bank, Bank Handlowy SA, would be privatised in the first half of next year.

"Poland's biggest commercial bank will be privatised in the first half of 1997," Kwasniewski said in a speech opening a two-day conference on investment opportunities in Poland organised by the International Herald Tribune.
Last month, the Polish government approved a banking privatisation plan which provides for selling Handlowy next year. But so far it has not given any indication about the timing of the sale.
The government also said the method of the privatisation was likely to be selected by the end of the year.

Kwasniewski also confirmed Poland's determination to start next year the privatisation of strategic and sensitive sectors such as telecommunication, energy and some companies from the defence complex.

Handlowy's net profit in the first half of this year rose 41.7 percent to 390.3 million zlotys from the same period of 1995. Its balance sheet total rose to 10.46 billion zlotys from 9.93 at the end of 1995 and 7.15 billion in mid-1995.
